summary: L-4 cab on the Coal Creek Mountain high point in Gifford Pinchot NF, used from 1934 and gone by the 1960s; reached on foot through the Goat Rocks Wilderness.

facts.design: L-4 cab on the summit, which replaced an earlier tent cabin
facts.status_note: Cab and earlier structure were gone by the 1960s; sources read describe no remains on the summit
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Gifford Pinchot National Forest

access.note: Reached on foot through the Goat Rocks Wilderness; the Bluff Lake road washed out in 2015

visit.trail_note: Coal Creek Trail, 6.5 miles one way with 3,600 feet of gain; a Packwood Lake route is a weekend trip

events.note: First used as an observation point with a tent cabin
Raymond Campbell on duty when lightning struck the cabin
L-4 cab replaced the tent cabin
Lookout welcomed 62 visitors that season, per a 1936 account quoted on the Forest Lookouts site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says the cab was removed in the 1960s; firelookout.com says destroyed in the 1960s; WillhiteWeb says both structures were destroyed by the 1960s. Story reports removed or destroyed and does not pick one.
FFLOS and firelookout.com give 6,359 ft (1,938 m) for the lookout; WillhiteWeb gives 6,376 ft as the summit elevation of the trail route. Record keeps the FFLOS figure.

sources.title: Lost Lake Lookout - Bluff Lake Trail

notes_for_editor: The 1931 lightning and 1936 visitor figures come from a Centralia Daily Chronicle report and a 1936 account as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not read. WillhiteWeb's summit elevation (6,376 ft) differs from the FFLOS figure. Removal wording differs (removed vs destroyed). No photos recorded.
